note: G3's x2.57 tax decomposed into a calibration-formula error, the junction C and the 100 mV gate-overdrive shift

checks.name: C1 the G matrix is tridiagonal (a chain of one-port flux elements)
checks.detail: largest non-tridiagonal entry 2.41e-10 S; diag/2 = 0.6929 mS equals the off-diagonal 0.6929 mS

checks.name: C2 the C matrix is diagonal to <1 % (node caps only)
checks.detail: max |C_ij| 8.10e-03 pF for i!=j, i.e. 0.76 % of C_ii

checks.name: C4 Y is quasi-static: G flat to 1 GHz and C flat from 1 kHz
checks.detail: G(1 kHz) vs G(10 kHz) 2.99e-10 S; C(1 GHz) vs C(10 kHz) 2.51e-05 pF (the FET channel RC does not roll the susceptance off)

checks.name: C5 the mode-1 eigenvalue matches 2(1-cos(pi/31)) (<2 %)
checks.detail: lambda_1*C/g 0.010150 vs analytic 0.010261 (-1.08 %); with a fully uniform C the matrix reproduces 0.010261 bit-for-bit, so the residual is the two measured C non-idealities: the end cap (1.0380 vs 1.0603 pF, +0.3 %) and the 0.76 % inter-node entries (-1.4 %)

checks.name: C6 the capacitance overhead is junction-only: C_ii/C_mim < 15 %
checks.detail: C_ii 1.0603 pF vs MIM 1.0163 pF = +4.3 % (260 aF of device caps per cell, not the x1.6 the G3 composition assumed)

checks.name: C7 the two-node cell has one dynamic node: g = 2*pi*f*C, not *2C
checks.detail: g_true 0.6929 mS vs G3's 1.3547 mS = x1.955 (the x2 is the formula, not the silicon: Vcal holds c1, only c2 integrates)

checks.name: C8 the 0.2 V chord probe is not a small-signal probe (different v_gs)
checks.detail: chord 1/1189 = 0.8410 mS vs g_ss 0.6929 mS = x1.21; the chord cell ties the source to 1.45 V (v_gs 1.85) while the chain sits at 1.65 (v_gs 1.65), and g is proportional to v_ov

checks.name: C9 a 0.1 V common-mode step costs ~20 % of g (low v_ov at v_sb=1.65)
checks.detail: g(1.65)/g(1.75) = 1.309; v_sb = 1.65 V raises Vth, so v_ov is only ~0.5 V and a 0.1 V gate swing is ~20 % of it

checks.name: C10 the G3 187.8 ns tail is reproduced in its own window (<3 %)
checks.detail: 188.8 ns vs the G3 record 187.8 ns (0.6 %) -- same netlist, same window

checks.name: C11 the 10 mV tail matches eig(G^-1 C) within 5 % (linear regime)
checks.detail: tau 154.1 ns vs eig 150.8 ns (2.2 %), fit residual 0.000

checks.name: C12 the 100 mV tail is slower by exactly the g(1.75)/g(1.65) ratio
checks.detail: tau100/tau10 = 1.271 vs g(1.65)/g(1.75) = 1.309 (-2.9 %) -- the step ends on a lower-overdrive bias, so the large-signal tail is the linear tail re-rated, not a different mode

checks.name: C13 the x2.57 tax is a product of three measured factors, not parasitics
checks.detail: x2.58 vs x2.67: calibration formula x1.96, junction C x1.04, gate-overdrive x1.31 (an UPPER bound: the tail sits between the 1.65 V start and the 1.75 V end, and the measured tail ratio is x1.27)

checks.name: C14 the true parasitic tax is the junction C alone (<10 %)
checks.detail: +4.3 % on C; with the 10 mV (small-signal) tau the residual over eig(G^-1C) is 2.2 %

checks.name: D1 tau_1(N) * lam1(N) = C/g at every N (the discrete mode-1 law, <3 %)
checks.detail: kappa spread 2.1 % over N = [2, 4, 8, 16]; lam1 = 2(1-cos(pi/(2N-1))) is the Dirichlet-Neumann eigenvalue, NOT 2(1-cos(pi/(2N)))

checks.name: D2 tau(16)/tau(2) equals lam1(2)/lam1(16) (within 5 %)
checks.detail: x100.6 measured vs x97.5 prediced by the mode law (log-log slope 2.22; a naive x64 assumes a continuum N^2)

checks.name: Ea tau_1 scales with the C-bank: MIM area + the fixed junction C (4x area -> 3.88x tau, within 5 %)
checks.detail: ratio to the 1 pF run 3.806 vs 3.875 (naive area ratio 4.0) -> -1.8 %

checks.name: Eb tau_1 scales with the C-bank: MIM area + the fixed junction C (16x area -> 15.38x tau, within 5 %)
checks.detail: ratio to the 1 pF run 14.991 vs 15.377 (naive area ratio 16.0) -> -2.5 %

checks.name: F1 the injected charge equals sum C_ii dV within 3 % (Q bookkeeping)
checks.detail: Q 1.712 pC vs 1.690 pC (1.30 %); the linear sum is C(n2..n16) + C(n1), and the residual is the junction Q(V) nonlinearity, not a leak
